items.title: A favourite Burger King for Mississauga residents closes as Chick-fil-A plans move ahead
items.summary: A longtime Burger King that has been a familiar stop for west Mississauga residents has closed, and its departure appears to be clearing the way for a new Chick-fil-A at the site. The restaurant was located at 2460 Winston Churchill Boulevard at the southwest corner of Dundas Street West. While technically an Oakville address, the plaza is a popular shopping destination for residents in both communities, particularly people living in west Mississauga. The Burger King closed without warning recently, and the building now sits empty awaiting its future. And that future likely is a conversion into a Chick-fil-A restaurant. The Town of Oakville continues to list the location as an active site plan application by Chick-fil-A. The plans call for the existing single-storey fast-food restaurant to be demolished and replaced with a new single-storey restaurant with a double drive-through. The application has also progressed since the proposal was first reported by INSAUGA Canada earlier this year. The town’s development file shows multiple rounds of submissions, including revised plans submitted in February and another round of documents submitted in April.

items.title: Man in Stable Condition After Stabbing at Square One Bus Terminal, Peel Police Say
items.summary: According to Insauga, Peel Regional Police were called to the Square One bus terminal in Mississauga on Friday night after reports of a stabbing. Police say the incident stemmed from an altercation between a man and a woman at the terminal near Square One Shopping Centre. The man suffered serious injuries in the stabbing, though his condition was later described as serious but stable. Officers took an adult woman into custody in connection with the incident, and police say there are no outstanding suspects they're looking for. A large police presence remained at the scene Friday night as investigators continued working the case. Police asked members of the public to avoid the area while the investigation was underway.

items.title: Gas Prices Set to Dip Sunday After G7 Agrees to Release 100 Million Barrels of Oil Reserves
items.summary: According to Metroland, Ontario drivers can expect a modest break at the pumps starting Sunday, according to Dan McTeague, head of Canadians for Affordable Energy. McTeague told Metroland that G7 countries agreed on Friday to release 100 million barrels of crude oil and petroleum product reserves over the next four months, with a particular focus on diesel, a move that pushed oil prices down on global energy markets. He explained that changes in energy markets typically show up at the pumps about two days later. Based on that pattern, McTeague predicts gasoline prices will actually rise by about seven cents a litre on Saturday before dropping roughly five cents on Sunday. The prediction follows a rockier stretch for local drivers, who saw prices jump a combined 14 cents over the two days before the G7 announcement. McTeague made his forecast Friday afternoon after energy markets had closed for the day.

items.title: Crombie Says She Was Told to Withdraw From Race Before Reporting Threat to Police
items.summary: According to Insauga, Peel Regional Police are investigating an alleged threat made against former Mississauga mayor Bonnie Crombie, who is running to reclaim the office in this fall's contentious mayoral race. Police told Insauga that Crombie filed a complaint on Sept. 21 about threats she received on social media, though investigators wouldn't disclose further details about the nature of the threat or the status of their probe. Crombie told Insauga she was contacted by someone who told her to withdraw from an upcoming debate, and said she knows the individual's identity but declined to name them publicly. She said she has since learned that the debate itself may also be targeted by an effort to have it cancelled outright. That debate is being hosted by Policorner, an organization that covers politics and related news at Queen's Park. Crombie, along with Mississauga councillors Alvin Tedjo and Dipika Damerla, has confirmed she'll take part, while Mayor Carolyn Parrish has turned down the invitation, citing other commitments.

items.title: Tedjo's Plan to Freeze Property Tax Hikes for Longtime Seniors Dominates Mayoral Debate
items.summary: According to Mississauga.com, the sharpest exchange at the Oct. 1 Food Banks Mississauga mayoral debate centred on a proposal from city councillor Alvin Tedjo to freeze property tax increases for longtime senior homeowners. Under Tedjo's plan, announced two days before the debate, Mississauga residents 65 and older who have owned and lived in their home for at least 20 years and don't own other properties would stop paying future property tax increases, with those deferred amounts collected by the city only when the home is eventually sold or transferred. Seniors already qualifying for the city's Low-Income Senior and Disability Property Tax Rebate would still be able to access that separate program. Former mayor Bonnie Crombie pressed Tedjo on how the city would cover the lost revenue in the short term and argued the program would need to be means-tested rather than open to all qualifying seniors regardless of income. The debate, moderated by CityNews' Mark McAllister and hosted in partnership with the Metamorphosis Network, was originally meant to focus on affordability, food insecurity and the rising cost of living, issues the food bank says are driving record numbers of residents through its doors. Beyond the tax proposal, the 90-minute debate between Crombie, Mayor Carolyn Parrish, Tedjo and councillor Dipika Damerla also drifted at points into personal attacks and crosstalk among the four candidates.

items.title: Nearly Half of September's School Zone Charges Were for Speeding, Peel Police Say
items.summary: According to Insauga, Peel Regional Police laid 1,034 charges during a school zone enforcement campaign that ran across Mississauga and Brampton from Sept. 8 through Sept. 30, with roughly half of those, 495 tickets, issued for speeding. The annual Back-to-School Traffic Safety Campaign was led by the force's Road Safety Services Bureau and focused on protecting students, families, crossing guards and school staff during the return-to-school period. Deputy Chief Marc Andrews said school zones full of kids and parents should be among the safest places in the community, yet officers keep encountering drivers who speed, run stop signs and engage in other dangerous behaviour. Andrews added that the results show road safety is a shared responsibility and that choices made behind the wheel can have serious consequences for children and families. Police said in a Friday news release that although this particular blitz has wrapped up, enforcement doesn't stop, calling proactive traffic enforcement a year-round effort to keep roads safe for everyone. The campaign is part of a broader push by Peel police to curb dangerous driving near schools as students return for the fall term.

This makes Mississauga 173rd out of 181 Ontario communities for car insurance affordability. However, insurance costs in Mississauga are lower relative to the premiums in Brampton, the most expensive city in the region at $3,802 per year. 2% higher. Car insurance premiums depend on many factors, such as the number of claims in an area, the amount of time drivers spend on the road, and each driver’s personal and insurance history. items.title: Crombie Says Beating Ford Would've Been 'Great for Mississauga' as Old Rivalry With Parrish Resurfaces
items.summary: According to Insauga, Thursday night's second Mississauga mayoral debate turned personal as Mayor Carolyn Parrish and her predecessor Bonnie Crombie traded sharp jabs, reviving a rivalry that dates back to a 2011 city council race between the two. City councillors Alvin Tedjo and Dipika Damerla also took part in the 90-minute debate, hosted by Food Banks Mississauga and the Metamorphosis Network at the food bank's east-end warehouse. Parrish, who won a mayoral byelection in June 2024 after Crombie left to lead the Ontario Liberals, questioned her rival's motives for wanting the job back. Crombie told Insauga it would have been "great for Mississauga" had she defeated Premier Doug Ford in the February 2025 provincial election, framing her failed run for the top job as something she pursued on the city's behalf. Much of the debate saw the two trade criticism over who would be more dedicated to serving as mayor, with Tedjo and Damerla also weighing in on the issues raised. The event marked the second of the campaign's mayoral debates as the Oct. 26 municipal election approaches.

items.title: City-Run Program Offers Mentorship and Investor Access to Mississauga Firms Ready to Scale
items.summary: According to the City of Mississauga, IDEA Mississauga, the city's business innovation hub, is accepting applications for its Step-Up Program, a six-month initiative aimed at companies that have already gained market traction and are ready to grow further. The program connects participating founders with executive training, mentorship, investor access and expert guidance meant to help them raise capital, enter new markets, build out their teams and strengthen operations. Participants join a cohort of other founders and work directly with experienced executives and industry experts, combining hands-on support with peer learning and tailored business advice. The city says Step-Up is aimed specifically at companies in the life sciences, advanced manufacturing and technology sectors, including artificial intelligence, clean technology and defence technology. Step-Up follows IDEA Mississauga's broader mandate of supporting local businesses through various stages of growth rather than just at the startup phase. The city is framing the program as a way to help high-potential Mississauga companies become more competitive as they move into their next stage of growth.

items.title: Peel Police Trace Missing Brampton Man's Movements From Pearson to a City Bus Near Airport Road
items.summary: According to Mississauga.com, Peel Regional Police are searching for a missing 44-year-old Brampton man identified only as James, whose surname has not been released by investigators. Police say James was dropped off at Toronto Pearson International Airport on Sept. 30 but never boarded his scheduled flight. Investigators say he was seen leaving the airport around noon that day and boarding a local transit bus. Police say he got off that bus near the intersection of Airport Road and American Drive, the last confirmed location investigators have for him. No additional details about his flight, his destination, or why he left the airport instead of boarding have been released. The case remains an active missing-persons investigation for Peel Regional Police.

items.title: Mississauga Man Held in Custody Nearly a Year After Puslinch Township Shooting
items.summary: According to Insauga, Ontario Provincial Police have charged a Mississauga man and two others with attempted murder in connection with a shooting that happened nearly a year ago in Puslinch Township, south of Guelph. Police say someone was shot in the early morning hours of Nov. 16, 2025, during what investigators describe as a home invasion, and the victim was taken to a trauma centre and later recovered. Two suspects were arrested in June, and a third was taken into custody on Sept. 9 as the investigation continued. OPP identified the Mississauga suspect as 20-year-old Lavontae Bowleg, who faces attempted murder with a restricted or prohibited firearm along with conspiracy, discharge of a firearm with intent, breaking and entering, and possession of property obtained by crime over $5,000. Bowleg remains in custody and is due in Guelph court on Oct. 9. An 18-year-old co-accused from Oshawa, who was a youth at the time of the shooting and cannot be named under the law, faces a similar set of charges. Police did not say in the release what led investigators to connect the three suspects to the shooting.
